origin.source_snapshot: Current customized working tree, with the Linux Gradle shell wrapper stored with LF and its tracked execute permission.

artifact.tested_artifact: Windows artifact reloaded into Burp Community 2026.11.2 without a binary change during finalization

build_environment.parameters: Offline, one Gradle worker, no persistent daemon or build cache, 768 MiB Gradle heap. Ubuntu used in-process Kotlin compilation and one test fork capped at 384 MiB.

verified_functionality: Streamable HTTP MCP connection, original tool schemas, and tool discovery
Global query, form, JSON string and supported multipart text parameter rewriting
Typed JSON request and response field matching and optional JSON Pointer rules
Complete eligible HTTP/1.1 and TLS HTTP/2 response body rewriting and compatible literal text
Combined request and response rewriting with independent masters
Exact-host allowlist, Burp Target Scope, local approval, and rule persistence
Shared approval dialog enable, denial and cancellation
Emergency Disable pass-through and stable counters on the final JAR
known_limitations: Visible compression passes through. Burp response unpacking must be disabled to arm response rewriting.
HTTP/1 chunked-origin identity is lost when Burp strips framing before Montoya. Some normalized chunked responses can be rewritten.
Montoya exposes processed HTTP/2 responses without raw frame completion or original trailer boundaries. Buffered compatible content can remain eligible.
Unsupported media, encodings, charsets, partial and conditional responses, downloads, streaming media, and malformed or oversized bodies pass through as documented.
WebSocket history Unicode may render incorrectly and affect regex matching. This release documents the limitation.
